subject: PilotWave urgent: sustained 504/429 surge during pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Omar Khan <omar.khan@pilotwave.ai>; Elaine Brooks <elaine.brooks@pilotwave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: PilotWave urgent: sustained 504/429 surge during pilot

Omar / Elaine —

Thanks for flagging. We see the same pattern on our side: starting ~08:45 PDT today your tenant saw a sustained increase in 5xx (predominantly 504s) and a concurrent uptick in 429s. High-level numbers from our dashboard: peak 504 rate ~18% for the tenant, sustained 504s at 7–10% for ~35 minutes; 429 spiked to ~7% and stayed elevated during the same window. P50 latency for the route increased from ~120ms to ~650ms and P99 shot to multi-seconds. Throughput also dropped as upstream retries queued.

We've attached a short bundle of logs (pilotwave_logs.zip) and a sample error batch (error_sample.txt) to help triage. Can you confirm the scope on your side (which services/apps were hitting the endpoint during the window) and provide a direct engineering contact for an immediate dig-in?

CCing Monica (CS/ops) and Evelyn (customer success) from our side — they can coordinate a call and handle account communication while we triage. Recommend an immediate short call (15–30m) so we can align mitigations (rate-limits, temporary retry backoff, possible model-variant fallback).

We realize this is disruptive during your pilot — we want to get a mitigation in place quickly and follow with a root-cause analysis.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: pilotwave_logs.zip, error_sample.txt

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PilotWave urgent: sustained 504/429 surge during pilot

Thanks Marissa — adding SRE/eng now. Omar/ELAINE — we appreciate the quick heads up. For the immediate call, who's the best engineering contact on your side? If you can share a short list of transaction IDs or a request sample (we got some in error_sample.txt but more samples help), we'll bring targeted traces and a timeline.

TL;DR of what we're seeing from preliminary logs attached: sudden increase in front-end queue depth followed by batch executor timeouts. Early hypothesis: a prefix-cache eviction or prefix churn that caused late KV cache lookups + larger-than-expected batching windows to overlap, driving queueing and retry amplification.

Proposed immediate actions we can effect from our side in the next 15–30m:
- Apply tenant-level rate limiter on the affected route (soft 20% throttle)
- Reduce maximum batch size for the tenant to 8 -> reduces tokenization bursts
- Temporarily disable prefix caching for the model variant serving the pilot (quick rollback path ready)

Attaching logs and a short timeline in timeline.xlsx. Vivek / Aditya — handing to you for a quick triage and to confirm if these mitigations look safe to execute.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PilotWave urgent: sustained 504/429 surge during pilot
To: Omar Khan <omar.khan@pilotwave.ai>, Elaine Brooks <elaine.brooks@pilotwave.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Vivek / Aditya — quick summary and findings from a ~10min read of the logs:
- Observed repeated KV-cache misses for the same prefix groups, followed by aggressive client retries; miss rate climbed sharply at the same time P99 jumped.
- Batching windows overlapped during high concurrency spikes; the batch coalescer held requests longer to hit configured batch size, increasing tail latency. When the cache misses returned larger payloads, executor queues filled and triggered 504s.
- Retry storm: the client-side SDK retried aggressively (no jitter) after transient 504s, amplifying queue depth.

Immediate ask: can you validate whether PilotWave SDKs were running an older retry policy, or if they were concurrently replaying requests? Also confirm if recent model-variant toggles or deployment pushes happened ~08:30–09:00 PDT.

Quick mitigations we should consider (safe, reversible):
1) Deploy tenant-level rate-limiter rule (20% soft throttle) — quick config change.
2) Reduce batch-size and reduce max batching window from 200ms -> 40ms for tenant.
3) Disable prefix KV-caching for the model variant serving PilotWave for the next 2 hours; fallback to stateless path.
4) Enforce retry-backoff at API gateway for that tenant (add jitter + exponential backoff).

If you approve, we can run 1–3 immediately in the next 15m as a canary on a single rack and monitor error-rate/latency. I'm also attaching a short error sample and the timeline.

—Monica

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PilotWave urgent: sustained 504/429 surge during pilot — quick mitigation plan

Thanks Monica — team looked through the traces and the attached logs. Confirming the hypothesis: a combination of prefix-cache churn and batching-window overlap caused executor queuing followed by timeouts when downstream KV service hit a hot partition. Key notes:
- Root trigger appears to be a KV partition hot-spot (metadata shows a sudden spike in key lookups for the same prefix group).
- Our batch-coalescer, configured to wait up to 200ms to form larger batches, compounded tail latency under the hot partition.
- The PilotWave SDK's retry behavior (no jitter, aggressive immediate retry x3) amplified the backpressure.

Immediate mitigation (rolling canary within 10–20m):
- Action A: Reduce batch-size to 8 and set max batch wait to 40ms for PilotWave tenant.
- Action B: Disable prefix KV-caching for the variant serving the pilot (stateless path) — immediate rollback path tested.
- Action C: Apply tenant-specific soft rate-limit and gateway retry policy with exponential backoff + jitter.

We will execute A+B on a single canary rack, monitor 1m/5m error rates and queue depth, then roll to remaining racks if green. Aditya will coordinate the change and monitor.

If the canary fails to improve error rates within 10m, we will switch the tenant to a smaller model variant with lower memory/kv-dependence as a precaution and engage you to coordinate messaging.

Markus — flagging for exec visibility; this may require a short SLA carve-out or credit conversation depending on root cause and impact duration.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Production Engineering
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: PilotWave — remediation actions taken and next steps (daily sync invite)

Omar / Elaine — quick update and next steps following the mitigation run yesterday:
- We executed the canary and applied reduced batch size + lowered batch wait and temporarily disabled prefix caching for your model variant.
- Error-rate and latency improved within the canary window: 504s dropped from peak 18% -> <1% on the canary, global tenant errors reduced to ~2% during the controlled rollout.
- We applied gateway retry jitter and a soft tenant throttle to prevent immediate re-amplification.

Next steps:
1) Post-incident RCA: our production eng team is running a deeper analysis on the KV partitioning and batching heuristics. We'll share a full RCA by EOD tomorrow (JIRA-RED-1287).
2) Permanent mitigations we're proposing: smarter prefix-cache eviction logic, adaptive batching (reduce batching when cache hit-rate drops), and a tenant-aware retry-shepherd at the gateway.
3) Daily sync for the next 3 days to monitor stability — proposed time 10:00 PDT. Invite attached.

We apologize for the disruption during your pilot. If you'd like us to shepherd communications to internal stakeholders at PilotWave, we can run a short exec summary for you.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — our team will follow up with the RCA and action items.

Best,
